comments.body:
Stronger variant observed on `80a5-cbb1-ef06-4ba5`: the gate does not merely fail to emit a sidecar — it presents a **stale** sidecar as the current one.

Timeline, all 2026-11-01 PST:

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 20:58:22 | review writes `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar, verdict BLOCK, 6 findings |
| 21:05:35 | ticket description rewritten, remediating all 6 |
| 21:05:52 | review run 1 → `status: failed`, `verdict: gate_congested` |
| 21:17:32 | review run 2 → `status: passed`, `verdict: BLOCK` |

After run 2, `gate_status` reported:

```
"findings": {"readable": true, "reason": "current-review-result-sidecar",
             "reviewed_at": "1793595502884924704"}
```

`1793595502884924704` is 20:58:22 — 19 minutes before the run it is attributed to, and 7 minutes before the description it supposedly reviewed existed. A directory listing of the ticket's tree on `origin/tickets` confirms only one sidecar exists; neither post-rewrite run wrote one.

Reading that sidecar's contents confirms it is the pre-rewrite review: its finding ids are exactly `fa8ebf20ba9d0a2c8`, `f53d891eb8f59d07d`, `f607dd457c67f9209`, `fae8752b49b276160`, `fc523973249550de7`, `f2083f043e6c4eab9` — the six already addressed by the 21:05:35 edit.

This is more damaging than the missing-sidecar case already described. A missing sidecar is visibly missing. A stale one labelled `current-review-result-sidecar` reads as authoritative, so the caller remediates findings that are already fixed, re-runs, and is handed the same list again. The loop terminates only if someone compares the sidecar timestamp against the job id.

It also makes the reported `verdict` untrustworthy. With no sidecar written by either post-rewrite run, there is no way to tell from the response whether `verdict: BLOCK` was decided by that run or echoed from the 20:58:22 sidecar. That distinction is not recoverable from the API output.

Two acceptance criteria to add:

- [ ] A findings sidecar is reported as current only when it was produced by the run being queried. Checked by: a test querying a job whose run emitted no sidecar while an older one exists, asserting `readable` is false rather than surfacing the older sidecar.
- [ ] A reported `verdict` is attributable to the queried run. Checked by: a test asserting the response distinguishes a verdict decided by this run from one carried over from a previous sidecar.

comments.body:
Root-cause investigation, 2026-11-03 (read-only; no code changed, not claimed). The divergence the gate reported was real. The "in sync" measurement in the description was taken on a different clone.

## Observation (MCP host, read-only SSM + journald)

- The gate reads the MCP server's clone (`/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`), not the operator clone the description measured. The description's reflog (`FILE_IMPACT adc7` at 21:14:28, resets at 21:14:11 and 21:15:13) does not appear in the server clone's reflog.
- Server clone, 2026-11-01 PST: `HEAD` reset to `4f4238a940` at 21:00:05, then 10 local `COMPACT` commits from 21:03:13 to 21:34:49, none pushed. Meanwhile `origin/tickets` fast-forwarded by fetch to `6e33ae7db2` (21:06:15), `7e85fc356c` (21:14:51), `81b4b14286` and `17d873220c`. `HEAD` merged it at 21:35:01. From 21:06:15 to 21:35:01 the clone had genuinely diverged (common ancestor, neither contains the other). `stale-store` / DIVERGED was a true report.
- The writer was one compaction sweep (`op=compact-sweep`, pid 1427). It held the store write lock 100-165 s per ticket and pushes only at the end of the sweep.
- Job records (`.rebar/gate_runs` on the host):
  - b505 (`weaponed-handheld-centipede`): job 21:00:15 to 21:11:32, PASS, `sidecar_emitted: false`. Signing failed at 21:08:30 with `PlanReviewGenerationRetryable: flock: could not acquire lock after 181s ... op=compact-sweep`; the sidecar emit failed at 21:11:32 with the same lock timeout.
  - 2041 (`golden-convergent-boutu`): job 21:00:21 to 21:10:36, BLOCK, `sidecar_emitted: false`; sidecar emit failed at 21:10:36 on the same lock timeout.
  - 80a5 run 2: job 21:17:32 to 21:19:50 (138 s), BLOCK, `sidecar_emitted: false`, `sidecar_reviewed_at: 1793595502884924704`. That is the `verdict_reuse` shape (`reuse.py`), not a fresh review. The 21:05:26 description edit (`6e33ae7db2`) was in `origin/tickets` but not in the clone's diverged `HEAD`, so the review read the pre-edit description, its material fingerprint matched the 20:58:22 sidecar, and the stored BLOCK was replayed.
- `gate_runs._review_result_status` labels any `sidecar_reviewed_at` it can find on disk as `current-review-result-sidecar`, including the prior timestamp the reuse paths copy in.

## Root causes

1. Compaction starves writers: `_sweep_should_yield` probes whether the lock is HELD between tickets, when the sweep has just released it, so a waiting writer is invisible. Reproduced locally across processes: the writer timed out after 3.03 s, and all 6 yield probes returned False. Filed as `radiant-benighted-warbler` (discovered_from this ticket).
2. The sweep's batched push leaves the clone genuinely diverged for the length of the sweep (same new bug).
3. A plan review runs, and bills, against a store the claim gate would refuse as stale, so it can review stale material and replay a stale verdict.
4. The findings status cannot distinguish a sidecar this run wrote from one a reuse path replayed.
5. `_uncertified_plan_review_reason` names `sign-review` even when no PASS sidecar exists to sign from.

## Consequence for the acceptance criteria

- The DIVERGED-predicate criteria (in sync never DIVERGED, mid-sync) rest on a misreport that did not occur. Not checked: whether `_ref_divergence`'s 4 sequential probes, each re-reading `HEAD` and the remote ref, can misclassify a ref that moves between them.
- The "sidecar written even when attestation cannot be persisted" criterion already holds in code (`_finalize_signature` records the signing failure without raising, then the emit runs). In the incident both writes failed on the same lock, so a test of that criterion as written would pass on current main.

comments.body: Operator decision 2026-11-03 (scope): requirement — the client must be able to run offline without knowledge of the remote store. Rescope this ticket to the plan-review side: (a) review-plan refuses, before any LLM call or charge, only when the clone is provably BEHIND or DIVERGED from its already-fetched remote-tracking ref (purely local check, freshness.py; never-fetched/no-remote = fresh); (b) unpublished local writes (push-pending marker) no longer make the store stale for ANY gate — review-plan, claim (gates.py store_freshness) and close (close_precheck assert_gate_store_fresh) — so an offline client can review, claim and close after local writes; accepted trade-off: a certificate can cover events the shared store has not yet received; (c) job status labels a reused/replayed REVIEW_RESULT as replayed and says whether this run decided the verdict; (d) the failure message suggests sign-review only when a PASS result file exists. The 2 DIVERGED criteria are dropped (the Nov 1 DIVERGED report was accurate; the lock fix is radiant-benighted-warbler, landed 25bce6c0550). The 'result file written even when signing fails' criterion already passes on main and is dropped.

comments.body:
Supersession record for the push-pending gating (implementation in progress, worktree fix-overweak2).

Push-pending refusal at every gate came from 3 tickets, all closed:
- `cibophobic-moist-guineafowl` (b928-3ab6-5985-417b): the deployed MCP clone could not push, so a valid completion attestation read as `unsigned` on a clone that never received it. Commit `2598909d25a` added `rebar._store.freshness` with 3 stale states: push-pending, behind, diverged.
- `yummy-yogic-clam` (2d52-5abe-abb8-44ab): stranded agent writes; the trailer on `2598909d25a` and `710a606b6d3` (write-side no-common-ancestor refusal, which this change keeps).
- `abnormal-dear-shoveler` (16c9-a42d-fd01-48b9): a stale marker wedged every gate after one failed push. Commit `8c5687af946` added `_pending_reconciled` / `_head_is_level_with` to discharge a marker that git disproved.

Why the 2026-11-03 decision supersedes them: b928's harm was a clone that had NOT RECEIVED shared writes (behind), and that case stays refused. Push-pending is the opposite case. The clone holds every shared event plus its own, so its view is a superset, not stale. Refusing on it made rebar unusable offline, against ADR 0045 and the operator requirement. The accepted trade-off is that a certificate can cover events the shared store has not received yet. With the marker no longer consulted by any gate, 16c9's wedge cannot recur, so its reconciliation helpers are deleted rather than kept as dead code. The marker is still written by `push_state.record_failure` and still reported by fsck (`PUSH_PENDING` from `_tracker_sync_status`), and `tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_push_pending.py` passes unchanged.

Scope note: `tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py` also changed. Its 2 tests pinned the unconditional `sign-review` advice, and they now stub a recorded PASS to keep their original intent.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

On 2026-11-01, 3 plan reviews were billed and lost. One review ran against a clone that had genuinely diverged from `origin/tickets`, so it read a superseded description and replayed an old BLOCK. `gate_status` then labelled that 19-minute-old `REVIEW_RESULT` as `current-review-result-sidecar`. The failure reason also told the caller to run `sign-review` when no PASS result file existed, so that command could not succeed. The root-cause comment of 2026-11-03 has the evidence. The compaction lock that caused the divergence is fixed separately (`radiant-benighted-warbler`, landed `25bce6c0550`).

Operator decision, 2026-11-03: **the client must be able to run offline without knowing anything about the remote store.** Today a clone with unpublished local writes cannot review, claim or close. `store_freshness` (`src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:174`) reports `push-pending` as stale, and every gate refuses on that. This rescope supersedes that part of `cibophobic-moist-guineafowl` (b928), `yummy-yogic-clam` (2d52-5abe-abb8-44ab) and `abnormal-dear-shoveler` (16c9-a42d-fd01-48b9). Accepted trade-off: a certificate can cover events the shared store has not received yet.

## Approach

1. **Push-pending no longer makes a store stale.** In `store_freshness`, drop the `elif pending:` branch (`freshness.py:222`) and remove `push-pending` from `_STALE_VERDICTS` (`freshness.py:45`). Delete `_pending_reconciled` and `_head_is_level_with` (`freshness.py:99`, `:129`), which exist only to discharge the marker for that branch; `grep` finds no other caller in `src/`. The marker itself is untouched. `push_state.record_failure` still writes it, and `fsck` still reports `PUSH_PENDING` (`fsck_tracker_health.py:215-227`). Behind and diverged remain stale, decided by the existing purely local `_ref_divergence` (`freshness.py:69`). It returns `None` when the remote-tracking ref does not resolve, so a clone that was never fetched, or has no remote, counts as fresh. All 3 gates call `store_freshness`: the claim gate (`attest_gate.py:133`), the plan-review close gate (`gates.py:204`) and the completion close gate (`close_precheck.py:681` through `assert_gate_store_fresh`). The one change therefore covers all 3, and none of the call sites needs editing.
2. **review-plan refuses a behind or diverged clone before any LLM call.** In `_run_plan_review` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`), call `store_freshness` after `collect_plan_relation_snapshot` (`:382`, whose `force_fresh` sync is the review's only network step) and before `assemble_context` (`:413`). When the store is not fresh, return an unsigned INDETERMINATE verdict built by `claimability.indeterminate_verdict` (`claimability.py:127`). It carries finding id `stale-store`, `coverage.llm_ran: false`, `signature.reason: "stale-store"` and the freshness reason, and exits 2. The check runs even with `--force`, because a forced review would still certify stale material. This placement reuses the existing early-verdict builder, the same one the not-claimable fast-fail uses, so the refusal costs nothing.
3. **gate_status labels replayed results.** `_gate_sidecar_fields` (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:162`) records `verdict_replayed: true` when the result's `runner` is `"reused"`, as set by both `reuse.verdict_reuse` and `reuse.idempotent_reuse`. Otherwise it records `false`. `_review_result_status` (`src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:243`) then reports reason `replayed-review-result-sidecar` instead of `current-review-result-sidecar` for a replayed run. Both reasons add `decided_by_run`: `false` for a replay, `true` for a run that emitted its own sidecar, and `null` for records written before this field existed.
4. **sign-review advice only when a PASS exists.** `_uncertified_plan_review_reason` (`attest_gate.py:99`) names `rebar sign-review` only when `sidecar.latest_review_result` (`sidecar.py:147`) returns a payload whose `verdict` is `PASS`. Otherwise it names only `rebar review-plan`.
5. Update the module and `store_freshness` docstrings in `freshness.py`, and the docs: `docs/concurrency.md` §stale-store (`:639`, which lists push-pending as stale) and `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (review-plan's stale-store refusal, the offline posture, and the `gate_status` findings fields next to `findings.readable` at `:794`).

## Scope

- src/rebar/_store/freshness.py
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py
- src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py
- src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py
- docs/concurrency.md, docs/plan-review-gate.md
- tests/unit/test_gate_store_freshness.py (update the push-pending tests)
- tests/unit/test_offline_gate_freshness_529c.py (new)

Out of scope: the compaction lock (`radiant-benighted-warbler`) and the `_ref_divergence` predicate itself.

## Testing

All tests are written to fail first, and none uses an autouse fixture. Each uses real git clones (an origin, a tracker and a second writer), as `tests/unit/test_gate_store_freshness.py` already does.

- Happy path: a clone that is ahead of `origin/tickets` and carries a push-pending marker passes the claim gate, the plan-review close gate and the completion close gate's freshness assertion. The same holds for a level clone with a marker. A clone with no `origin/tickets` ref, and one with no remote, also pass.
- Failure path: a clone that is behind, and one that has diverged from its fetched ref, are refused by all 3 gates with `stale-store`. `_run_plan_review` on a behind clone returns INDETERMINATE `stale-store`, and a runner stub that raises proves no LLM call was made.
- Replay: a `gate_status` record whose result has `runner: "reused"` reports `replayed-review-result-sidecar` with `decided_by_run: false`. A fresh run reports `current-review-result-sidecar` with `decided_by_run: true`.
- Advice: with no sidecar, or only a BLOCK sidecar, the claim-gate reason omits `sign-review`. With a PASS sidecar, it includes it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An ahead or level clone carrying a push-pending marker passes all 3 gates' freshness checks. Checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_offline_gate_freshness_529c.py -k push_pending`.
- [ ] A behind or diverged clone is refused by all 3 gates with verdict `stale-store`. Checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_offline_gate_freshness_529c.py -k "behind or diverged"`.
- [ ] `review-plan` on a behind or diverged clone returns INDETERMINATE `stale-store` with no LLM call. Checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_offline_gate_freshness_529c.py -k review_plan`.
- [ ] A clone with no fetched ref, or with no remote, counts as fresh. Checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_offline_gate_freshness_529c.py -k "no_fetch or no_remote"`.
- [ ] `gate_status` labels a replayed result `replayed-review-result-sidecar`, with `decided_by_run` reported. Checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_offline_gate_freshness_529c.py -k replay`.
- [ ] The claim-gate reason names `sign-review` only when a PASS `REVIEW_RESULT` exists. Checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_offline_gate_freshness_529c.py -k sign_review`.
- [ ] `fsck` still reports `PUSH_PENDING` for an ahead clone with the marker. Checked by `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_push_pending.py` passing unchanged.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0, and the freshness, gate, close-precheck, MCP and plan-review test modules pass. Checked by running them with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.

file_impact.reason: push-pending no longer stale; drop marker reconciliation helpers
refuse a behind/diverged clone before any LLM call
name sign-review only when a PASS REVIEW_RESULT exists
record verdict_replayed on the gate job record
label replayed sidecars and report decided_by_run
document review-plan refusal and replay labels
update tests that pinned push-pending refusal
